slides.title: Progression Is Built, Not Accumulated
bullets: Moving from MSL toward greater responsibility isn't automatic with years of experience
It's a deliberately built progression, applying leadership competencies visibly
This happens while still executing the current role with excellence

slides.title: Expand Your Scope of Impact Gradually
bullets: Start by excelling in your own territory and relationships
Then proactively seek ways to contribute beyond that individual scope
Examples include leading a process improvement or coordinating team-wide congress prep
These opportunities often have to be actively sought and proposed

slides.title: Make Your Work Visible to Decision-Makers
bullets: Excellent work that stays invisible to leadership doesn't translate into progression
Communicate your own results and contributions effectively
Apply the executive communication and impact narrative principles from this course

slides.title: Seek Mentorship From Those Already There
bullets: Identify professionals already in the type of role you aspire to
Proactively ask what competencies and experiences mattered most in their own progression
This practical knowledge is something no theoretical course fully replicates

slides.title: Stay Anchored to the Function's Purpose
bullets: Progression is more sustainable when it's not about titles or formal authority
Think of it instead as an expanding capacity to contribute to better clinical decisions
The same purpose that opened this course should guide every step of the trajectory

slides.title: Apply It With Consistency and Ambition
bullets: This course covered the technical, relational, strategic and digital knowledge behind this trajectory
Applying it with consistency, honesty and genuine ambition is now your responsibility
The path runs from the first field visit to leading an entire medical organization

takeaway.title: Progression from MSL to Medical Lead is a deliberately built trajectory, not a reward for tenure
bullets: Expanding your scope of impact and making it visible both require proactive effort
Mentors who've already made this progression offer knowledge no course can replicate
Staying anchored to the purpose of better patient outcomes keeps the trajectory sustainable
